It is the highest -tier output artifact MGE can produce — and it only unlocks when the MQ6 Trust Score reaches 85 or above (the Certified zone, TG11 pass condition, R135/R146). Each word, in context: • Court -Admissible — The architecture is designed to satisfy three Federal Rules of Evidence: FRE 803(6) (business records exception), 902(11) (self -authentication of business records), and 1002 (best evidence rule). "Court - admissible" describes the architec tural intent; the CAAR is engineered so a legal team can introduce it as evidence without requiring FohBoh to provide live testimony about how the number was calculated. The chain of custody, the immutable Vault record, the narrative hash, the attestation block, and now the Section 11 master system attestation are all designed to satisfy those standards by architecture. Important caveat: FohBoh does not make blanket court -admissible guarantees. A narrowly scoped legal opinion is required before that claim i s made in a specific proceeding. • Analysis — The CAAR is not a raw data export. It is a structured analytical document: it includes the full Trust Gate evaluation table, the certified variance calculation with rule IDs, the chain -of-custody log, the evidence bundle references, and the cert ification attestation block. It tells the story of how the certified number was reached, in language a non -technical reader (attorney, judge, arbitrator) can follow. • Report — A formatted, finalized document artifact. Not an API response. Not a dashboard widget. A document with a hash, a date, an attestation block, and an Evidence ExportPack that travels with it. The 85 -Threshold Below a score of 85, MGE still produces certified outputs — variance figures, Trust Score summaries, certified PDFs. Those are operationally valuable. But only the CAAR carries the full evidentiary apparatus: the attestation block (R149), the CAAR - specific SHA-256 hash (R150), the Evidence ExportPack (R151) with every source file, normalized record, and Audit Trail extract bundled together, and the master system attestation (R198). The 85 threshold exists because below that score, at least one Trust Gate is failing or significantly penalized — meaning there is a material gap in the evidence chain. A CAAR produced on incomplete data would not survive a competent challenge. The thresho ld is the integrity floor, not an arbitrary gate. The commercial implication is significant: the CAAR is what turns a certified variance number into a dispute instrument. A franchisor can take a CAAR to a franchisee in an arbitration proceeding. A restaurant can take a CAAR to a DSP's legal team in a fee dispute. Without the CAAR, you have a number. With the CAAR, you have evidence. Evidence ExportPack structured index document inside the bundle — the table of contents that makes the pack legally coherent rather than just a folder of f iles. When an operator requests an ExportPack alongside a CAAR (R151), MGE assembles a ZIP archive containing seven categories of material: • Source files — original ingestion files exactly as received (DSP statement, processor statement, POS export, contract exhibit). Unmodified. • Normalized records — the canonical -schema output from the ingestion pipeline. Proves the transformation was rule-governed, not interpretive. • Certified calculation record — the KPI Vault output. Shows which formula version was active, what inputs were applied, what certified output was produced. Immutably locked with its SHA -256 hash. • DCLS output — the full narrative artifact produced by the Certification Language System, with its narrative hash attached. • CAAR — the Court -Admissible Analysis Report itself, including the Trust Gate evaluation table, variance calculation, and attestation block. • Audit Trail extract — a time -stamped log of every processing event in the certification pipeline: ingestion receipt, normalization, rule execution, Trust Gate evaluation, output production. Every event has a timestamp and an operator attribution (R182). • Manifest — the document that ties all of the above together: inventory with integrity hashes, chain -of-custody declaration, rule -to-evidence mapping, certification metadata summary.
